elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Section 11.1 permits Customer to terminate the Agreement during the Term for convenience.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: Customer must provide at least ninety (90) days' written notice.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: The rendered language contains no obligation to refund prepaid fees pro rata.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: M&I's no-cause withdrawal right is effective only at the end of the then-current Term; the immediate termination language is tied to a regulatory, legislative, or judicial trigger rather than convenience.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Section 11.1 permits convenience termination on at least ninety (90) days' written notice.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: The Termination for Convenience Fee is expressly limited to an amount not exceeding three months' Fees, and the additional cost pass-through was removed.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: M&I's unilateral withdrawal of non-Core Services is effective only at the end of the then-current Term; immediate termination is separately conditioned on a regulatory, legislative, or judicial event.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: M&I must provide ninety (90) days' prior written notice for its unilateral withdrawal right.
